slides.title: Enums – Named Constants 📛
slides.content:
# Making Magic Numbers Meaningful

An **enum** (enumeration) is a set of named integer constants. They make code more readable and less error‑prone.

```csharp
public enum Direction { North, South, East, West }
```

Now you can use `Direction.North` instead of remembering a number or string.

Under the hood, enums are integers (default starts at 0). You can assign custom values:
```csharp
public enum Difficulty { Easy = 1, Medium = 2, Hard = 3 }
```

quizData.question: Why use enums over strings for something like direction?

options.text: Enums prevent typos and are type‑safe

quizData.explanation: Enums ensure you use only predefined values and catch mistakes at compile time.

slides.title: Enum in Inspector 🖥️
slides.content:
# Editor-Friendly

A public enum variable shows up in the Inspector as a dropdown list, making it easy to configure objects without coding.

```csharp
public enum EnemyType { Melee, Ranged, Boss }
public EnemyType type;
```

You'll see a dropdown in the Inspector to select Melee, Ranged, or Boss. Extremely useful for designers!

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Iterating Enums

You can loop through all enum values using `foreach (MyEnum val in Enum.GetValues(typeof(MyEnum)))`. This is great for populating UI dropdowns.
